title: A Statistical Approach to Machine Translation
authors: P. Brown, J. Cocke, S. Della Pietra, V. Della Pietra, F. Jelinek, J. Lafferty, R. Mercer, P. Roossin
before: Translation systems were hand-built rule sets, one language pair at a time.
problem: Rules could not cover the variety of real sentences and did not transfer between languages.
breakthrough: Treat translation as a probability problem learned from aligned corpora rather than a rule problem.
why: It moved the whole field from hand-written knowledge to learned statistics, the assumption everything later rests on.
next: Class-based n-grams, then two decades of statistical MT that neural translation eventually displaced.
inherits: The conviction that data beats hand-crafted rules.
